name.en: Jacob Blessing the Sons of Joseph

provenance.assertion: Hessen Kassel Heritage states that Landgrave Carl chose Hercules as a symbol of his power and had the monumental statue erected.
provenance.qualification: The relation records patronage/commissioning; it does not assert that Carl personally designed the monument.

provenance.assertion: UNESCO states that the monumental water displays were begun by Landgrave Carl from 1689.
provenance.qualification: This relation denotes initiation of the Baroque water-display project, not sole design authorship of every later water feature.

provenance.assertion: The ICOMOS evaluation says Carl appointed Guerniero to take charge of the design; the Kassel catalogue attributes the 1713 pyramid design for the Octagon to Guerniero.
provenance.qualification: The place node represents the Hercules/Octagon monument ensemble rather than a single drawing.

provenance.assertion: ICOMOS places Guerniero in charge of the design of Carl's Baroque water-display project, whose Grand Cascade is the principal surviving axis.
provenance.qualification: This is a design-lead relation for the Baroque project, not a claim that all later cascade alterations are Guerniero's work.

provenance.assertion: Hessen Kassel Heritage states that Wilhelm IX had the Löwenburg built between 1793 and 1801.
provenance.qualification: The relation records the patron/commissioner role, not architectural authorship.

provenance.assertion: Deutsche Biographie explicitly identifies Jussow with the planning of Löwenburg; the Kassel drawing catalogue preserves attributed Löwenburg designs by him.
provenance.qualification: The relation concerns the designed Löwenburg complex and does not imply sole execution of every later restoration phase.

provenance.assertion: The Kassel catalogue attributes the Aqueduct design GS 5727 to Jussow and notes that the depicted Aqueduct already corresponds closely to the execution begun in 1788.
provenance.qualification: A separate first proposal is documented as unexecuted; this relation relies on the later design associated closely with the executed Aqueduct.

provenance.assertion: The Kassel catalogue attributes to Jussow a circa-1791 plan of the Pluto Grotto, Höllenteich and Devil's Bridge landscape setting.
provenance.qualification: This deliberately does not encode unqualified authorship of the present bridge; the evidence establishes Jussow's design role for the earlier landscape/site phase.

provenance.assertion: Jussow's circa-1791 plan documents the reworked landscape composition around the existing Pluto Grotto, Höllenteich and Devil's Bridge.
provenance.qualification: The Plutogrotte predates this plan, so the relation is to its landscape setting rather than original authorship of the grotto.

provenance.assertion: Hessen Kassel Heritage lists Der Segen Jakobs among the celebrated Rembrandt works in the Old Masters collection.
provenance.qualification: No acquisition or commission history is inferred from this attribution.

provenance.assertion: The official collection page names Der Segen Jakobs as a Rembrandt work in the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister.
provenance.qualification: The relation records current collection membership only.

provenance.assertion: Hessen Kassel Heritage states that the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister has been housed in Schloss Wilhelmshöhe since 1974.
provenance.qualification: The stable graph place id schloss represents Schloss Wilhelmshöhe; no content-id migration is introduced.

provenance.assertion: The official Schloss Wilhelmshöhe gallery page names Der Segen Jakobs among the Rembrandt paintings shown in the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister there.
provenance.qualification: This models the museum display/location relation and does not infer ownership or acquisition history.
